purpose: Close the native subagent alias refusal gap from merged124 with no new refusal policy, live calls or permission changes.
mechanism: tools/ask-model.mjs agyBuildDenials first groups every subagent conversation_id/log_uri pair named together anywhere in raw step updates, using smaller-to-larger alias groups, then folds each final identity updates in original stream order through the unchanged classifier. This preserves denials seen before a late identity link and preserves paired later nonpermission errors that supersede an unpaired earlier message. Parent step logic, all-result denials, sanitized 64-entry bounds, model-mismatch precedence, read-only wall/auth/token rules and model proof stay unchanged. docs/neon-builder.md describes the stream grouping. Tests now10alias cases plus existing suites; originalcounterexamples and nonpermissioncasepass independently injudge recheck.
decisions: Identity-only link placement cannot affect the same chronological update fold; moving a state/message-bearing update naturally changes chronological input. No new refusal kinds, matching rules, fields read from output text, transcriptIO, sandbox defaults or liveprobe. Originalapproval-filenameLOW remains filed; do not imply every ENOENT is unconditionally clean if message matches existing approval pattern. Other124filedLOWs untouched. No Bsavedexclusion claims or liveconfiguration.
readers: docs/neon-builder.md is for CLI operators/orchestrators. Source comments tell maintainers why identity grouping precedes the fold, not implementation narration. Current build records are immutable evidence, not editorial docs.

docMap.behavior: Canonical subagent identity grouping and original chronological refusal fold
